claim: BRIDGE3R is a causal camera--human bridge built on a Human3R-derived recurrent reconstructor.
caveat: The contribution is the same-scene boundary operation; do not claim dense-scene improvement or backbone independence.

claim: On EgoBody, BRIDGE3R improves recording-macro W-MPJPE, WA-MPJPE, ATE-Sim3, and IDF1 over continuous-state Human3R while retaining local body quality.
caveat: Use all 43 recordings and 129 cases; preserve paired uncertainty and identical-coverage accounting.

claim: On identical EgoBody RGB clips, BRIDGE3R has higher complete-denominator IDF1 and Coverage than executable TRACE and PromptHMR-SPEC references.
caveat: TRACE and PromptHMR geometry is conditional on method-specific finite support; this is not an equal-temporal-access or common-support ranking.

claim: On the fixed EgoHumans 90-clip protocol, BRIDGE3R improves W-MPJPE, WA-MPJPE, ATE-SE3, and IDF1 over continuous-state Human3R.
caveat: All paired point estimates use the same 90 clips; Coverage changes from 0.639 to 0.616 and must remain visible.

claim: The same configuration improves WA-MPJPE, ATE-Sim3, and IDF1 over continuous-state Human3R on the Harmony4D 88-case protocol.
caveat: Do not claim all-metric dominance: W-MPJPE increases from 496.6 to 519.6 mm and Coverage decreases slightly.

claim: Across the dataset-equal macro, gains are larger on the pre-defined extreme/farthest-view subsets than across all views.
caveat: Report every dataset and retain the unresolved Harmony4D extreme-view W result; do not claim monotonicity with angle.

claim: BRIDGE3R exceeds HumanMM or Multi-THuMBS under a common executable protocol.
caveat: Use protocol-level literature context only; do not insert source-paper values into a same-input result table.

claim: BRIDGE3R preserves emitted history and composes across repeated same-scene boundary events.
caveat: Real repeated-cut evidence contains four Harmony4D streams and belongs in the supplement; it is not a large multi-cut benchmark.

claim: BRIDGE3R handles arbitrary cross-scene edited video or improves dense scene geometry.
caveat: Restrict claims to same-scene viewpoint cuts and camera--human consistency.

claim: The new MVHuman captures provide positive evidence that the automatic detector correctly bridges weak-texture hard cuts.
caveat: The detector fires early in 40/50 streams; retain the 50-case result only as a supplementary end-to-end availability/failure audit and do not replace detection with the annotated boundary.

claim: GVHMR is a full-denominator MVHuman baseline.
caveat: The pre-specified 12-case pilot completes 10/12 and fails its expansion gate; do not report its ten-case conditional geometry as a leaderboard.

claim: BRIDGE3R outperforms PromptHMR on the held-out MVHuman stress protocol.
caveat: PromptHMR completes 50/50 and has lower anchor and seam-root errors, while BRIDGE3R has lower relative camera-rotation error. PromptHMR is offline and BRIDGE3R's causal proposal fires early in 40/50 cases; retain the result only as a supplementary availability/failure audit.
